site.title: Cosmos Person
site.lede: Nebulae, galaxies, and the occasional comet — photographed one clear night at a time.
site.statement: The light in these photos is old — some of it left home before humans figured out writing. Then it fell into my telescope. That still gets me every time.

images.title: The Wizard Nebula
images.description: An open star cluster carving shapes into the cloud it was born from. With a little imagination there's a wizard in there — pointy hat and all.

images.title: The California Nebula
images.description: A hundred-light-year ribbon of hydrogen, glowing under UV light from the star Menkib. Named for its shape, not its weather.

images.title: The Butterfly Nebula
images.description: Wings of glowing hydrogen split by a dark dust lane, wrapped around Sadr — the bright star at the heart of Cygnus.

images.title: The Ghost of Cassiopeia
images.description: Gas and dust slowly getting blasted away by the star Gamma Cassiopeiae next door. It genuinely looks like a ghost mid-drift.

images.title: The Whirlpool Galaxy
images.description: A spiral galaxy caught tugging on its smaller neighbor, NGC 5195. The gravitational tug-of-war lights up new stars along its arms.

images.title: The North America Nebula
images.description: Dark dust lanes carve a surprisingly good map of North America into this huge cloud of glowing hydrogen near Deneb.

images.title: The Pinwheel Galaxy
images.description: A face-on spiral nearly twice the size of the Milky Way, dotted with enormous star-forming regions.

images.title: Thor's Helmet
images.description: A bubble blown by a Wolf-Rayet star — a massive sun burning hard and fast before it goes supernova. The wings are a bonus.

images.title: The Horsehead Nebula
images.description: Probably the most famous silhouette in the sky: a pillar of cold dust a light-year tall, backlit by glowing hydrogen.

images.title: The Pacman Nebula
images.description: A busy star-forming pocket in Cassiopeia. Tilt your head and it's clearly mid-chomp.

images.title: The Soul Nebula
images.description: A huge stellar nursery in the Perseus Arm, hollowed out by the winds of its newborn star clusters.

images.title: The Eastern Veil Nebula
images.description: The eastern edge of the Cygnus Loop — the still-expanding shockwave from a star that blew up thousands of years ago.

images.title: The Eagle Nebula
images.description: The Pillars of Creation and the Spire rise from a cavern of ionised gas, mapped in the Hubble palette.

images.title: The Lagoon Nebula
images.description: A giant star-forming cloud in the heart of the Milky Way, its hourglass core lit by the young cluster NGC 6530.
